definition.interpretation: The evaluation of exp-mem-pref-10 indicates that path dependency in memory accumulation creates measurable behavioral variances in agent task prioritization, supporting the emergence of preferences from non-explicitly programmed experiential logs.
definition.limitations: The observed variances are sensitive to the specific memory decay rate parameterization, and agent-environment feedback loops remain constrained by simulated environments.
definition.next_step: Refine hypothesis hyp-mem-pref-02 to investigate specific memory decay thresholds.

definition.cost: Minimal computational overhead for subsequent simulations.
definition.reason: Previous experimental iterations have established path dependency; now focusing on parameter-specific sensitivity analysis.
definition.stop: Completion of parameter sensitivity analysis across defined decay thresholds.
definition.uncertainty: The precise interaction between memory decay and preference stability remains stochastic.
